Commentary.Commentary: Daren Ganga is taking an interview of Alzarri Joseph. The fast bowler says that he first felt that the pitch looked dry and hence, was just looking to hit the right areas around the stumps. Is not too fussed about when the ball is given to him but wants to do well as and when it is given. Admits that the bounce is inconsistent in this pitch, so batsmen will find it difficult to get adjust. On his return from injury, Joseph says that he does not think about that injury and just concentrates on playing cricket. Is pretty confident that West Indies can chase this total down.

Now then, the Windies bowlers have done their job now it is onto their batters to chase this down. They should back themselves but the wicket is a little tricky, if the Irish bowl well, they could well be in with a chance. Do join us but before that, Joseph is seen giving an interview.

The Windies bowling wasn't that great to begin with, however, the introduction of Joseph changed all of that, he along with Chase got rid of the top order. Cottrell then got a couple in his second spell. Walsh also had two to his name however, the pick was Joseph who finished with a four-fer.

A poor, poor display with the bat by the visitors! Not what their skipper would have wanted after they elected to bat. They though started off quite decently however, once Stirling fell, they kept losing wickets at regular intervals. They were reeling at 88 for 6. A 50-plus run stand though between Tucker and Adair gave some respectability to the score. However, both fell in quick succession and little contribution from the lower-order meant the visitors are well short of where they would have wanted to be.

We are all set to begin. The West Indies players are out in the middle. Paul Stirling and the debutant Gareth Delany will open the batting for Ireland. Sheldon Cottrell will start the proceedings for the hosts.
West Indies (Playing XI) - Shai Hope (WK), Evin Lewis, Shimron Hetmyer, Brandon King, Nicholas Pooran, Keiron Pollard (C), Roston Chase, Keemo Paul, Hayden Walsh, Alzarri Joseph, Sheldon Cottrell.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Gareth Delany (DEBUT), Andrew Balbirnie (C), William Porterfield, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Kevin O'Brien, Mark Adair, Simi Singh, Barry McCarthy, Andy McBrine, Boyd Rankin.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of the visitors. Ireland have won the toss and have elected to bat first.

A warm welcome to the first ODI between West Indies and Ireland in Bridgetown. The hosts would look to start 2020 in a positive note. They would look to improve their performance from their last series against India. On the other hand, Ireland would look to begin with a confident manner. They have a good batting line-up and can give a tough fight to the hosts. Stay tuned for the toss and the teams.
